# Modelly

> Modelly is an open-source Python framework for agent-based modeling: agents with a step(), state in numpy columns, grids, networks, continuous and geographic space, seeded reproducible runs, experiments, calibration, sensitivity analysis, decisions, a model hub and a browser Studio.

Install with `pip install modelly-abm`. Every page below is also served as Markdown; all of them in one file: https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/llms-full.txt

## Guides

- [Modelly: agent-based modeling in Python](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/index.md): Modelly is an open-source Python framework for agent-based modeling (ABM): agents in numpy columns, grids, networks and continuous space, seeded reproducible runs, calibration, a model hub, and 2.9 to 135 times the speed of Mesa 3.5.
- [Getting started](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/getting_started.md): Start with Modelly, the Python agent-based modeling framework: install it, build a first model in a tutorial, then find the guide, example or API page for what you want to do next.

## Course

- [Course: agent-based modelling with Modelly](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/index.md): Twelve sessions that take a class from a first model to a validated, reproducible study of its own, with a model card and a comparison that a decision can…
- [Session 1: agents, a scenario and a step](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_1.md): Know the three pieces of a Modelly model: a Scenario (the inputs), agents, and a Model with a step.
- [Session 2: data, seeds and reproducibility](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_2.md): Collect model-level data with a DataCollector and turn it into a pandas DataFrame.
- [Session 3: space, rasters and percolation](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_3.md): Put a model on a grid, and number its cells with a CellIndex so that a whole-landscape question (“which trees touch a fire?”) is one sparse product.
- [Session 4: networks and contact structure](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_4.md): Represent who-influences-whom as a network, and an influence step as one sparse product.
- [Session 5: thinking in arrays, columns and cohorts](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_5.md): Store the attributes that are updated in bulk as Columns, and update the whole population with numpy.
- [Session 6: validation against theory](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_6.md): Zoo models: age-structured SEIR, Nagel-Schreckenberg, Bass diffusion
- [Session 7: experiments, sweeps and replications](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_7.md): Design a parameter sweep with replications, each run with its own independent seed.
- [Session 8: from the zoo to your own project](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_8.md): Start a project from a zoo model and change it into the model of a question of your own.
- [Session 9: model cards and the hub](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_9.md): Zoo models: Boltzmann wealth exchange, within-host and between-host epidemic
- [Session 10: decisions, strategies and costs](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_10.md): Zoo model: age-structured SEIR, through the vaccination study of modelly.decide.vaccination
- [Session 11: causes, effects, attribution and counterfactuals](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_11.md): Zoo model: Bass diffusion, and the virus-on-a-network example bundled with Modelly (modelly.examples.basic.virus_on_network)
- [Session 12: continuous dynamics inside agents, and the final projects](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/session_12.md): Give every agent its own ODE with modelly.couple.AgentODE: the state variables are columns, and the whole population is integrated as one batch.
- [Instructor notes](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/instructors.md): Notes for teaching the twelve sessions, one 2-hour slot each, and the assessments: the rubric of the final project and two short graded exercises with their…
- [From NetLogo: a track for instructors](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/course/from_netlogo.md): This page is for instructors who teach agent-based modelling with NetLogo and want to move a course to Modelly. It maps the NetLogo concepts to Modelly, shows…

## API reference

- [APIs](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/api_main.md): One page per domain package of modelly: core, space (with space.geo and space.networks), population, time, data, behaviour, scenarios, experiments, calibrate…
- [Core](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/core.md): modelly.core holds the model, agents, agent sets, columns, the random source and the exceptions. modelly.Model, modelly.Agent, modelly.Column and…
- [Space](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/space.md): modelly.space holds the discrete cell spaces (grids, networks, Voronoi meshes), continuous space, property layers and the integer cell index. The names most…
- [Geospatial space](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/geo.md): modelly.space.geo needs the optional geo extra (pip install "modelly-abm[geo]"); download_osm also needs the osm extra. The guide is Geospatial models.
- [Networks](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/networks.md): modelly.space.networks holds the temporal and multilayer networks, contact matrices, network statistics and importers. It needs only numpy and scipy; NetworkX…
- [Synthetic populations](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/population.md): modelly.population builds people, households, places and contact networks from aggregate tables. It needs numpy and pandas; locate_households takes a GeoSpace…
- [Time](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/time.md): modelly.time holds the event list, events and event generators, the scheduling methods of the model, and signals (observables that notify subscribers when…
- [Data](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/data.md): modelly.data holds two ways to collect data from a run: the DataCollector (model, agent, agent-type and table reporters, called once per step) and the dataset…
- [Behaviour](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/behaviour.md): modelly.behaviour holds building blocks for what agents do: timed actions, continuous states with thresholds, and meta-agents (agents made of other agents).
- [Scenarios](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/scenarios.md): modelly.scenarios describes the parameters of a run as a typed Scenario (with its seed), runs many scenarios and keeps their results in a Store.
- [Experiments](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/experiments.md): modelly.experiments runs parameter studies: a space, a design, replicates and outputs, on any executor, into a resumable Parquet store. How to use it is in…
- [Calibration](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/calibrate.md): modelly.calibrate fits parameters to observed data. How to use it is in Calibration.
- [Sensitivity](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/sensitivity.md): modelly.sensitivity ranks parameters by their influence. How to use it is in Sensitivity analysis.
- [Decisions](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/decide.md): modelly.decide compares, costs and stress-tests strategies. How to use it is in Decisions.
- [Causes and explanations](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/explain.md): modelly.explain estimates effects, attributes outcomes, replays counterfactuals and computes Shapley values. How to use it is in Causes and explanations.
- [Model cards](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/card.md): modelly.card writes, checks and stamps model cards. How to use it is in Model cards.
- [Model hub](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/hub.md): modelly.hub finds, installs, publishes and checks models on the hub. How to use it is in The model hub.
- [Bindings for R and Julia](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/bindings.md): modelly.bindings holds the plain functions the R package (r/modelly) and the Julia package (julia/Modelly.jl) call. How to use them is in From R and Julia.
- [Coupling](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/couple.md): modelly.couple couples agents to fields, ODEs and stock-flow models. How to use it is in Coupling agents with fields and ODEs.
- [Emulate](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/emulate.md): modelly.emulate fits emulators to a model’s runs, chooses runs by active learning and rules out parameters by history matching. How to use it is in Emulators.
- [Batch](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/batch.md): modelly.batch runs many independent model runs and holds counted populations.
- [GPU](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/gpu.md): modelly.gpu runs column phases, cohort tables and cell-space operators on numpy, CuPy or JAX, with counter-based random numbers that are the same on every…
- [Differentiable models](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/diff.md): modelly.diff simulates models written as JAX phases and differentiates their outputs with respect to their parameters. How to use it, and when the gradients…
- [Viz](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/viz.md): modelly.viz draws models in the browser and in notebooks. The names most models need are exported by the package itself: from modelly.viz import SolaraViz…
- [Time travel](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/timetravel.md): Recording, rewinding, branching and diffing runs. How to use them is in Time travel and run diff.
- [Studio](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/studio.md): Modelly Studio, the browser app behind modelly studio. How to use it is in Modelly Studio.
- [Web](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/web.md): Modelly in the browser: modelly export-web and the Python its pages run in Pyodide. How to use it is in Modelly in the browser.
- [logging](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/log.md): It is modeled on the default logging approach that comes with Python.
- [Migrate](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/migrate.md): The Mesa to Modelly codemod behind python -m modelly.migrate. The construct-by-construct map is in Migrating from Mesa.
- [Lint](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/lint.md): The static checks behind python -m modelly.lint. The rules, with examples, are in Lint.
- [Profile](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/profile.md): The runtime profiler behind python -m modelly.profile. How to read its report is in Profiling a model.
- [Provenance](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/provenance.md): Manifests, verification, bundles and ODD skeletons behind modelly run, modelly verify, modelly bundle and modelly odd. How to use them to publish a study is…
- [LLM](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/llm.md): Language-model agents: the client, its cache, budgets, retries, providers and structured decisions. How to use them is in Language-model agents.
- [Plugins](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/plugins.md): modelly.plugins finds third-party extensions through package entry points. The guide is Plugins.
- [Model zoo](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/zoo.md): modelly.zoo is the catalogue of reference models; the guide is Model zoo. Each model is in modelly.zoo.<name>.model.
- [Distributed](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/distributed.md): One model split across processes or machines (provisional, new in 1.4), with the same results as one process for the same seed. The guide is From laptop to…
- [Stream](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/apis/stream.md): Live observations for running models (provisional, new in 1.4): sources that hand out observations as they arrive, observation operators that read the same…

## Roadmap

- [Roadmap](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/index.md): Status: 1.3 released, 1.4.0 in release (every epic merged except F10 Studio II, release gate pending) · Current release: 1.3.3
- [1.3.0: answers and trust](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/1.3.0.md): Status: released as 1.3.0, with fixes in 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and 1.3.3 · Base: 1.2.0
- [1.4.0: scale out and connect](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/1.4.0.md): Status: in release: every epic merged except F10 Studio II (in progress), release gate pending · Base: 1.3.3
- [1.5.0: ecosystem and collaboration](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/1.5.0.md): By 1.5.0 a single researcher can build, calibrate, scale and publish a model. 1.5.0 is about everyone else: the colleague who wants to reuse it, the policy…
- [2.0.0: clean foundations](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/2.0.0.md): 2.0.0 is the only release on this roadmap allowed to break things, and it breaks them on purpose and with a map. Three 1.x releases of features leave behind…
- [Platforms: Windows, macOS and Linux](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/roadmap/platforms.md): Rule: a feature ships only when it works on Windows, macOS and Linux, with the same results for the same seed. A feature that cannot (for example, a SLURM…

## Design notes

- [Design reviews](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/design/index.md): A design review records, for one epic, what was decided, what else was considered and why the choice was made. The 1.3.0 roadmap asked for one page each for…
- [Design review: calibration (E1)](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/design/calibration.md): Scope: priors, targets, distances, the posterior object, the methods and how they run. Code: modelly.calibrate. Guide: Calibration.
- [Design review: sensitivity analysis (E2)](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/design/sensitivity.md): Scope: what is analysed, the parameter space, the methods, their estimators and results. Code: modelly.sensitivity. Guide: Sensitivity analysis.
- [Design review: language-model agents (E7)](https://remipelloux.github.io/Modelly/design/llm-agents.md): Scope: the client, providers, the response cache, budgets, structured decisions and how LLM runs stay reproducible. Code: modelly.llm. Guide: Language-model…
